findings.claim: R2-COR-MAJ-001 is confirmed closed against actual repo state at HEAD 24c8992 (fix-round-2 applied). All four inline-fix elements described in FIX-ROUND-2.md are present and correct: (a) WARN_BASELINE_RULES set in emitter heredoc; (b) denies counter excludes warn-baseline rule_ids; (c) verdict-derivation warn branch; (d) warn-baseline 4th fixture.
findings.evidence: (a) policy-check.yml 'Build scorecard emit' step line 1309: WARN_BASELINE_RULES = {"SCP-R-004"} — exact literal match to the render-deny step's WARN_BASELINE_RULES = {"SCP-R-004"} at line 973. Both are Python set literals with the identical single member. (b) policy-check.yml lines 1333-1337: denies counter conditional is 'if (verdict == "deny" and rid not in waived_rule_ids and rid not in WARN_BASELINE_RULES): entry["denies"] += 1' — the third clause 'rid not in WARN_BASELINE_RULES' is present and correctly excludes SCP-R-004 from the denies increment. (c) policy-check.yml lines 1369-1379: verdict-derivation block: first branch 'if any(v["denies"] > 0 for v in rule_counts.values()): verdict = "deny"'; second branch 'elif any(rid in WARN_BASELINE_RULES and v["raw_findings"] > v["waived"] and not v["rule_config_disabled"] for rid, v in rule_counts.items()): verdict = "warn"'; else 'verdict = "allow"'. Deny-first precedence is correct: an effective deny (post-suppression, post-warn-baseline-exclusion) dominates. The warn branch fires only when no effective denies remain and at least one warn-baseline rule has raw_findings > waived and is not rule_config_disabled. (d) tests/scorecard-emit/fixtures/warn-baseline/policy-check-summary.json: findings=[{rule_id:'SCP-R-004', verdict:'deny', file:'output/findings/waivers.json', message:'waiver entry 0 reason field must contain a decision-artifact URL'}]; waivers_applied=[]; disabled_rules=[]; bypass_emitted=false. tests/scorecard-emit/fixtures/warn-baseline/expected-scorecard-emit.json: verdict='warn'; rule_counts={'SCP-R-004':{raw_findings:1,denies:0,waived:0,rule_config_disabled:false}}; waivers_aggregate={active_count:0,by_rule_id:{},expiring_within_30d:0}; rule_config_aggregate={disabled_rules:[],expiring_within_30d:0}. Manual trace: waived_rule_ids={} (waivers_applied empty); for SCP-R-004: raw_findings=1, verdict='deny' but rid in WARN_BASELINE_RULES → denies stays 0; waived=0; rule_config_disabled=False. Verdict: any(denies>0)→False; warn branch: 'SCP-R-004' in WARN_BASELINE_RULES AND 1>0 AND not False → True → verdict='warn'. Fixture expectation matches computed result exactly.

findings.claim: No new CRIT or MAJ correctness findings from fix-round-2 deltas. All five fix-round-2 delta elements — WARN_BASELINE_RULES definition, denies counter exclusion, warn verdict branch, warn-baseline fixture pair, and release-notes rewrite — are each independently correct and mutually consistent.
findings.evidence: Delta element 1 (WARN_BASELINE_RULES definition in emitter, line 1309): literal {"SCP-R-004"} is a valid Python set. Dual-definition pattern (mirroring render-deny) is the established coupling contract and is documented in the code comment: 'Mirrors the WARN_BASELINE_RULES set in the workflow's render-deny step'. Delta element 2 (denies counter exclusion, lines 1333-1337): condition is a three-clause AND — verdict=='deny', rid not in waived_rule_ids (pre-existing from R1), rid not in WARN_BASELINE_RULES (new). For SCP-R-004 with verdict='deny' and no waiver: only the third clause fires to block the increment. For deny-baseline rules (SCP-R-001, SCP-R-002): neither in WARN_BASELINE_RULES, so clause is vacuously True and behaviour is unchanged. Delta element 3 (warn verdict branch, lines 1370-1377): 'rid in WARN_BASELINE_RULES' limits the warn trigger to warn-baseline rules only; deny-baseline rules cannot contribute to this branch regardless of raw_findings count. Condition 'v["raw_findings"] > v["waived"]' correctly checks for unsuppressed raw findings (not raw_findings > 0, which would incorrectly warn when all raw findings are waived). Condition 'not v["rule_config_disabled"]' correctly suppresses warn for rule-config-disabled rules. Delta element 4 (warn-baseline fixture, traced above in R3-COR-CLOS-001). Delta element 5 (release-notes rewrite, verified in R3-COR-PASS-002). Cross-fixture regression check: deny-with-waiver fixture (SCP-R-001 raw deny + waivers_applied=[SCP-R-001]): waived_rule_ids={'SCP-R-001'}; SCP-R-001 rid not in WARN_BASELINE_RULES (correct); denies=0 (blocked by waived_rule_ids); warn branch: 'SCP-R-001' not in WARN_BASELINE_RULES → False; verdict='allow'. Matches deny-with-waiver/expected-scorecard-emit.json: verdict='allow', SCP-R-001.denies=0, waived=1. ✓ Full fixture (SCP-R-001 waived, SCP-R-002 un-waived, SCP-R-003 no-manifest-applicable): waived_rule_ids={'SCP-R-001'}; SCP-R-001: denies=0 (waived); SCP-R-002: rid not in waived_rule_ids and not in WARN_BASELINE_RULES → denies=1; SCP-R-003: skip clause fires (reason=='no-manifest-applicable') → no entry; verdict='deny'. Matches full/expected-scorecard-emit.json: verdict='deny', SCP-R-001.denies=0, SCP-R-002.denies=1. ✓ No regression in any pre-existing fixture.

findings.claim: Release notes 'Workflow permissions delta' section accurately reflects the fix-round-2 state of the workflow.
findings.evidence: docs/releases/v1.2.0.md 'Workflow permissions delta' section (rewrote in fix-round-2 per CG-R2-MIN-002): states (a) new attest-scorecard job with attestations:write + id-token:write at JOB level NOT workflow default level; (b) job gated on 'if: inputs.scorecard-emit' AND 'needs: policy-check'; (c) workflow-level permissions unchanged: contents:read + statuses:write. Verification: policy-check.yml lines 56-66: workflow-level permissions block contains 'contents: read' and 'statuses: write' only; explicit comment states 'attestations: write or id-token: write' are absent at workflow scope. policy-check.yml lines 1610-1637: attest-scorecard job — 'name: scp/attest-scorecard'; 'if: inputs.scorecard-emit'; 'needs: policy-check'; 'runs-on: ubuntu-24.04'; 'permissions: {contents: read, attestations: write, id-token: write}'. Release notes claim (a)-(c) are each exactly correct against the workflow. The 'AND needs: policy-check' claim: verified at line 1613. The claim that 'opt-out runs never get the OIDC permissions granted at all' is accurate because the job-level permissions only activate when the job runs, and the job is gated on inputs.scorecard-emit.

self_reported_concerns: WARN_BASELINE_RULES dual-definition coupling: the emitter's WARN_BASELINE_RULES set is a local heredoc constant that must be manually kept in sync with the render-deny step's set. If a future engineer adds a 2nd warn-baseline rule to render-deny without updating the emitter, the verdict would be wrong ('deny' when the gate passed). This is a pre-existing structural concern documented by the code comment and TF-020P-001 (promote to data-driven manifest when 2nd rule lands). No new correctness risk from fix-round-2 — the fix correctly mirrors the render-deny pattern as designed. Not a blocking concern at v1.2.0 with only one warn-baseline rule.

warn-baseline fixture message simplification: warn-baseline/policy-check-summary.json uses a simplified 'message' string ('waiver entry 0 reason field must contain a decision-artifact URL') rather than the verbose format produced by SCP-R-004.rego ('SCP-R-004 waiver entry 0 (rule_id=..., finding_id=...): reason field must contain a decision-artifact URL...'). The emitter never reads the message field for logic — only rule_id and verdict are consumed. No correctness impact on the fixture's validity as an emitter test. Not a finding.
summary: R3 correctness review of WP-SCP-023 slice 023B at HEAD 24c8992 (fix-round-2 applied). All three R3 verification targets pass cleanly.
